subject: Nebular AI — GPU pool topology decisions and next steps
messages:
From: Lily Chen <lily@nebular.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-25T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: Dedicated pool for Nebular — topology & sizing questions

Hi Priyom / Monica,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Nebular is ready to move forward with a Dedicated GPU pool for inference (customer-facing chat + batch embeddings). Before we lock SOW timelines the engineering team asked for a short decision log so we can confirm region choices, autoscale/burst expectations, and minimal baseline topology.

Quick context:
- Production traffic: steady-state ~120 QPS (token generation) and peak spikes up to ~480 QPS for hour-long campaigns, usually once per day.
- Models: one LLM at ~30B params (FP16), one tiny reranker.
- Data residency: EU customers must be served from eu-west for PII handling.

As next steps we need:
1) Recommended minimal pool sizing and expected latency at 512-token average.
2) Autoscale and burst policy recommendation (how many GPUs reserved vs burst).
3) Confirmation on regions you can provision by mid-July (we prefer us-west + eu-west).

Attached a short requirements overview (nebular_requirements.pdf).

Can you confirm a quick agenda for a decision call tomorrow?

Thanks,
Lily
Head of Platform
Nebular AI

Attachments: nebular_requirements.pdf (PDF)

Hi Lily — thanks, and great to see the numbers. Proposed short agenda for tomorrow's call:

- Review Nebular steady/peak load and model footprints (5 min)
- Capacity topology options: single-region dedicated vs multi-region multi-pool (10 min)
- Autoscale & burst policy defaults and tradeoffs (10 min)
- Minimal acceptance criteria and timeline to provision a pilot pool (5 min)
- Actions and owners (5 min)

A few quick asks ahead of the call so we can bring realistic numbers:
- Average sequence length (tokens) for inference requests (helps with per-token latency numbers).
- Expected concurrency vs QPS (if known).
- Any special networking / private connectivity (VPC peering, private endpoints) requirements.

I've attached a working capacity matrix to fill (initial_capacity_matrix.xlsx) — if you can drop in model sizes + typical sequence length we will prepare pool-sizing options.

If tomorrow is tight we can do Friday — what time window works for you?

Cheers,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lily Chen <lily@nebular.ai>
Date: 2028-06-25T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated pool for Nebular — topology & sizing questions

Lily / team — adding a couple of operational guardrails we typically recommend for this profile:

- Baseline reserved pool: size for ~1.5x steady-state to keep tail latency stable; burst policy to allow 2x reserve for short windows (order-of-magnitude: reserve N GPUs, burst +N for up to 60 minutes).
- Prefer separate staging pool in same region for smoke tests and model swaps (helps rollouts).
- For EU residency: we can provision a eu-west dedicated pool and route EU clients to that pool — billing and quotas still consolidated.
- Default autoscale: aggressive downscale window 10–15m to avoid cost spikes, up to full burst within 2–3 minutes based on queue depth.

I'll bring sample numbers to the call based on the matrix Priyom sent.

—Monica
Senior CS Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lily Chen <lily@nebular.ai>
Date: 2028-06-26T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated pool for Nebular — topology & sizing questions

Looping in a couple of infra questions that will change the topology recommendation:

1) GPU family preference: do you require A100-class GPUs, or can you accept an H100 quantized runtime? H100 offers lower latency for large seq lengths but has slightly different driver/isolation considerations.
2) Multi-AZ or single-AZ? Multi-AZ gives higher availability but increases cross-AZ egress costs for KV caching and can affect latency SLOs.
3) Do you need private link for customer traffic or will public endpoints be acceptable behind private routing?

If Nebular prefers H100 + multi-AZ, our recommended pilot topology is: 8 H100 per region reserved, burst up to 16 for 30–60 minutes with prefix caching enabled. If they need strict EU-only routing with separate data controls we should do two fully isolated pools.

Quick ask to Lily: please confirm GPU family and whether you can tolerate a small cross-AZ egress allowance.

Thanks,
Karthik
Infra Lead, Dedicated Services
From: Lily Chen <lily@nebular.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-27T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated pool for Nebular — topology & sizing questions

Thanks all — quick answers from our infra team:
- GPU family: H100 preferred if supported; otherwise A100 is acceptable for the pilot.
- Multi-AZ: we prefer multi-AZ within a region for availability. We understand some egress costs may apply.
- Private connectivity: yes, we'll need a VPC peering/private endpoint to route customer traffic; we can share NetOps contact after the call.

Attached is a filled version of your capacity matrix with sequence lengths and per-request concurrency (initial_capacity_matrix.xlsx). Also looping Alex Torres (alex.torres@nebular.ai) who will own procurement/timing.

Timeline ask: can Redwood provision pilot pools in us-west and eu-west by July 18? That would let us start our validation run the week of July 22.

Lily

2) Karthik: scope network setup (VPC peering + multi-AZ details) and a short doc with expected cross-AZ egress impact. ETA: July 3.
3) Monica: draft SOW addendum options for reserved vs burst commitments and acceptance criteria for pilot. ETA: July 5.
4) Alex (Nebular): confirm procurement lead and sign-off window so we can prioritize capacity.

We can run a 30-min decision sync on July 6 to confirm choices — propose 09:00 PT. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include a short decision log template for capture.

Actions:
- Priyom to upload the proposed pool spreadsheet to the HubSpot deal and share a Doc link.
- Monica to draft SOW options.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot stood up.

Best,
Priyom
